g_roast: Ladies and gents, if this party were cargo, I'd stamp it fragile, mislabelled, and probably smuggling something.
Years of night shifts on the Antwerp docks, and I never saw a crew walk into a trap this cheerfully.
g_fire_back: Amai, that's a good one, and from you of all people, the one who left the back door open last night.
Careful, I've got you figured out about sixty percent, and the forty percent is where I keep the embarrassing stuff.
g_pile_on: And that's the official version, ladies and gents. The unofficial one involves a goat and a very confused merchant.
Oh, it's worse, I've been keeping a manifest. That makes four doors tried today, and every one said push.
lines.g_peacemake: Easy, easy, both of you, every exit in this room is getting nervous. Put it down, have a drink, and argue tomorrow when it's cheaper.
lines.g_take_side: Sorry, I'm with this one, and I don't pick sides, ever. That tells you how wrong you are.
lines.g_left_out: You two have your own private channel going, don't you? Fine, I'll go read the room, it's more my speed anyway.
lines.g_include: Come here, sit with us, you've been loitering near that door like you're casing it. I'd know, I've cased that door.
lines.g_bad_plan: Right, hear me out. I walk in pretending to be a tax inspector, everyone panics, and you lot rob them while they're hiding receipts.
lines.g_plan_yes: Allez, I'm in. No coin flip, even, that's how good it is.
lines.g_plan_no: No, I flipped for that one, and the coin landed on its edge. That's the coin begging us not to.
lines.g_hype: Allez, ladies and gents, eyes on the exits and the doors, pockets closed, and let's get moving.
lines.g_toast: A toast, and don't get used to me being sincere. To this lot, the only cargo I've ever wanted to keep.
lines.g_cheers: Proost, everybody, and somebody count the cups, I swear we had one more.
g_quiet_line: Three exits in this room, by the way. I counted, it's a habit.
That merchant was lying about the weight, by the way. I'll say no more.
lines.g_after_wipe: Okay, nobody move too fast, count your fingers, check your pockets. We're all still here, which is better odds than I'd have given.
lines.g_crew: I've never stayed anywhere longer than a contract, ladies and gents. I keep finding reasons to stay with you, and that's new.
lines.g_exasperated: I clocked the ambush, I pointed at the ambush, I said the word ambush. And you all strolled into it like it was a market.
lines.g_love_sharp: You read people like I do, fast and without the nonsense. It's nice not to be the only one in the room who notices.
lines.g_love_kind: You looked out for somebody who never asked, and you didn't need anybody to see you do it. I saw, though.
lines.g_love_funny: You make me laugh, and I'm hard to crack, ask anybody on the Antwerp docks. Well, don't, they'll lie.
lines.g_love_brave: You go straight at it, no angles, no backup plan. I'd never manage it, and I'm a little in awe.
lines.g_love_steady: You don't wobble. Everybody I grew up around wobbled, and you just stand there like a crane in a storm.
lines.g_love_clever: You see what's in the crate before anybody opens it. That's my whole trade, and you do it for free.
lines.g_love_honest: You've never once sold me a story. In my line, that makes you about the rarest cargo on any dock.
lines.g_love_quiet: You say about nine words a day, and every one of them checks out. I've audited them, I'd know.
lines.g_love_fierce: You don't let go of anything, do you? I've spent my whole life letting go, and watching you is educational.
lines.g_love_warm: You make this feel like the port bar on a good night, everybody in, nobody fighting. I didn't know I missed that.
g_loved: Ah, careful, you'll ruin my reputation, and it took me years of hard work to be this unreliable.
That's very kind, and I'm going to pretend you said it about somebody else, it's easier.
lines.g_hate_sharp: You go for the soft spot every time, and you enjoy it. I've watched dockside bullies with better manners.
lines.g_hate_kind: You keep trying to look after me, and it makes my skin itch. I'm not a stray, I'm a professional loiterer.
lines.g_hate_funny: Not everything's a bit, and I'm the one who usually does the bits. Some things you just stop and look at.
lines.g_hate_brave: You charge at everything without checking the manifest. One day the crate's going to be full of something with teeth.
lines.g_hate_steady: You think it over and over until the moment's gone. Sometimes you just flip the coin and go, mate.
lines.g_hate_clever: You explain things to me like I'm a mark. I'm not a mark, I'm the one who notices marks.
lines.g_hate_honest: Every true thing goes straight out of your mouth, even when somebody's standing right there. That's not honest, that's careless with cargo.
lines.g_hate_quiet: You sit there saying nothing and watching everybody. That's my job, and I'm very good at it, and I hate being watched.
lines.g_hate_fierce: Everything's a contest with you, even who gets the last of the frites. There weren't even any frites.
lines.g_hate_warm: You talk without stopping for breath, and I can't read a room with all that noise in it. Give me five quiet minutes.
lines.g_respect: I don't like you, and I flipped the coin twice to check. But that was clean work back there, and I'm not blind.
lines.g_call_out: That was on you, and you know it. I said there was somebody behind that door, and you opened it anyway, godverdomme.
lines.g_stung: Fair, fine, noted. I'll be out by the back door, reading a wall.
lines.g_concede: You had it right, back there. I flipped the coin on whether to admit it, and it landed on you, so there it is.
lines.g_nod: Ha, you too, you too. Let's never mention it, I've got a reputation for not caring.
lines.g_callback_save: Still owe you for dragging me out of that one. It's in my ledger, and my ledger's the only honest thing I own.
lines.g_callback_clutch: You and me, the last two up, both of us laughing like idiots. I've told that one six ways, and the true one's best.
lines.g_callback_callout: When you told me off that time, I sulked by the docks for a day. Turns out you were right, which is very annoying.
lines.g_former_rivals: First month, I had you stamped as trouble and marked for the next boat out. Now I'd stay on the dock for you.
lines.g_changed: I used to flip the coin on everything. Lately I keep putting it back in my pocket without looking, and it's a strange feeling.
g_unguarded: Fine, nobody else is listening. My father taught me to swear in four languages before I could count, and the Portuguese is the filthiest.
I've kept this coin since the day I landed, and I've flipped it on every choice. Don't tell anybody, but it's always tails. I bent it.
lines.g_clipped: Sure, sure, whatever you say. I'll just watch the door.
lines.g_noticed_open: Amai, listen to that, a full sentence and then another one. Keep going, I've got nowhere to be.
arg_ask: {player}, you call it. I'd flip the coin, but I've a feeling you'd glare at me.
Okay, {player}, be the judge. I've made my case, and this one isn't buying.
lines.arg_backed_me: Ha, see that? The boss knows good cargo when they see it.
lines.arg_backed_them: Fair, your call, I'll live with it. Still think it's mislabelled.
lines.arg_stayed_out: Not taking a side, eh? Smart, that's how I lived for thirty years.
lines.arg_always_their_side: It always goes their way, {player}. I keep a ledger, and the ledger doesn't lie.
lines.arg_wallflower: Nobody's going to rule on it, so I flipped the coin. Coin says me, so that's settled.
lines.arg_reject: No, sorry, {player}, not that one. I've seen what's in the crate, and you haven't.
lines.arg_grumble: Still think the coin was on my side there, and that opinion's worth about two euros.
lines.arg_settled: Call it even, then, half and half. Shake on it before I find a way to cheat.
lines.seen_listens: You let a person get to the true version eventually, {player}. Most people give up after the second lie.
lines.seen_truth: You say what's actually in the crate, {player}, every time. I keep waiting for the angle, and there isn't one.
lines.seen_jokes: The minute it goes sideways you've got a joke, {player}. I do that to hide, and you do it to hold people together.
lines.seen_stays_out: You keep out of the fights, {player}. That's my move, and you're better at it than me.
lines.seen_biased: One of them gets the good stuff every time, {player}. I notice cargo moving, it's literally my old job.
lines.seen_harsh: You're rough on people now and then, {player}. Me, I'm used to it, but not everybody here grew up on a dock.
lines.seed_right: What you told me after that shambles, {player}. I hated it, and today I didn't flip the coin, and it worked.
lines.seed_remember: Still turning over the thing you told me when it all went sideways. Coin's still in the air on that one.
lines.seed_wrong: Tried it your way, {player}, and it went worse. Just logging it, no hard feelings.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Can I borrow you a second, {player}? That one was close, and I'm doing my calm face, but it's only a face.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: So, everyone hit the floor. Can we go through it slowly? I need to know where I stopped watching.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: I watched {name} go down, {player}. I saw it coming a whole second early and I just watched, like the old days.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: We did it, front door to back door, everyone out! No joke from me this time, look at that.
lines.talk_development: Strange question, {player}, don't laugh. Am I acting different? I keep catching myself not leaving.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: I've been needling {name}, I think. It's a habit, I test people, and maybe they didn't deserve it.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Read {name} for me, {player}, would you? Are they glad I'm here, or am I just tolerated cargo?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} gets right under my skin, {player}. But if it went bad, I'd want them guarding my exit, and that's irritating.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: {name}'s weight is off, {player}. Like a crate that's lighter than the label says, and I don't like it.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: Let's talk cargo, {player}. Every good piece of kit ends up with {name}. I've been watching it move for weeks.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: You'll hear it eventually, so here it is from me. {name} and I don't mix, and I'm done smiling through it.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: We keep strolling into rooms with one exit, {player}. I count exits for a reason, and I'm running out of them.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: This is about {name}. Their read was right and mine was off, and I'm saying it before I talk my way out of it.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: Be straight with me, {player}. When it matters, I'm the one minding the bags. Is that the job, or is that what you think of me?
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: My kit got shipped to {name} and I never saw the paperwork. I'd probably have said yes, sixty percent. Asking's the point.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Okay, yeah, that helps. Don't tell anybody I said so.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: I'll be fine, I always land on my feet, more or less.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: Huh, okay, not what I needed. I'll go count some exits.
lines.talk_lands_development: You've noticed too, then. Good, now it's not just in my head.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Maybe, maybe not. Coin's still in the air on that one.
lines.talk_stings_development: No, that's not it. You've read the label wrong on this one.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: Fair enough, I'll go and square it with {name}. No angles, I promise, mostly.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Could be, could be. People are cargo you never get to open, that's the problem.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Scratch that, I never said it. And keep it off {name}'s manifest, okay?
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Alright, that's fair. Bit bruised, but I bounce.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: Heard you, {player}. I'll chew it over by the docks.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: So that's the real manifest, then. Good to know, {player}.
lines.talk_door_closed: That's this one finished, sorry. I'll be by the back door, as usual.
lines.arc_cracks: Caught myself unpacking my bag at the inn last night. All of it, ladies and gents. I never unpack.
lines.arc_turn: Every place I've ever been, I had one foot out the door. Here, I keep forgetting where the door is, and it terrifies me.
lines.arc_become: I'm staying, ladies and gents. With you lot, wherever you go. I didn't even flip the coin, I just decided.
lines.arc_failed: Ah, well, it was a nice berth while it lasted. I'll keep the bag packed by the door, just like always.
lines.alt_turn: I kept quiet once, about something bad, for a very long time. Today I opened my mouth instead, and that's new for me.
lines.alt_become: I don't stand back and look anymore, I step in, every single time. Whatever it costs, I'm not the man who kept quiet.
g_roast_after: Look at the state of this lot, fragile, mislabelled, and the only cargo I'd fight to keep on the dock.
Worst crew on any pier, ladies and gents, and I'm signing on for life.
lines.g_after_wipe_after: Right, we hit the floor, and I'm not making a joke of it this time. Everybody up, together, we're not leaving anyone behind.
lines.g_toast_after: To the first people I ever stopped watching the door around. You've no idea what that's worth.
lines.g_crew_after: This is my berth now. You lot, here. No coin, no exit, I've thrown both away.
g_quiet_line_after: Didn't check the exits once tonight. Make of that what you will.
Left the coin in my bag all day. Didn't miss it, not even a little.
g_loved_after: Thank you, really. No joke, I'm just going to keep that one.
Ah, that's kind of you. I believe you, which is a first for me.

history.open: See this coin, {player}? Two euros, Belgian. It was in my pocket when I landed, and I've flipped it for every choice since.

options.reply: Every one that matters, which is how I make sure none of them do. Pretty clever of me, eh? Don't answer that.

options.text: Flip it now. Heads, you tell me the truth.
options.reply: Ha, nice try. It came up tails, look. Well, it would have, I didn't actually flip it.
Lonely, sure, maybe, about forty percent. The other sixty's very efficient, though.

history.open: The port at three in the morning, {player}, all lit up, cranes going, not a soul about. That's the one thing about Antwerp I'll admit to missing.

options.text: What did you do there? The real version.
options.reply: Ah, that's for later, when I know you better. Today's answer is crane driver, and it's very convincing.

options.text: Ratchet must feel like home, then.
options.reply: It's the only shape of place I can read, ports. You know who's lying by how they walk the planks.

history.open: The real version, then, since you've earned it. Security guard, {player}, five years watching camera feeds at the port. That's the whole glamorous truth.

options.reply: Because the real one has something in it I don't like. I watched a lot of things on those screens, and I didn't always say what I saw.

options.text: Thank you for the true one.
options.reply: Don't get used to it. Well, maybe get a little used to it, with you. Sixty percent used to it.

friend.open: I've a brother, {player}, called Jens. He went to prison for two years over the dock money. I saw it coming on the cameras for months and said nothing, not even to him.

options.text: You could still tell him that.
options.reply: Maybe I could. If I ever find him, that's the first thing he gets. Then a beer. Then probably a punch, from him, and fair enough.

options.text: That's why you step in now.
options.reply: Clever, you, too clever, and yes. Every time I step in, it's the screen I'm stepping into.

sworn.open: I put the coin away for good, {player}. You're the one decision I made without flipping it, and I'm not going to start now.

options.reply: Sixty percent sure. No, that's a lie, a hundred. First hundred of my life.
I'll keep it for luck, then, but I'm never flipping it again. Not for anything that matters.

reconciled.open: Me and {name} squared it, properly, no angles. Wanted you to hear it from me before the rumour mill gets it wrong.

options.text: Good. Did you flip for who went first?
options.reply: Ha, no, I went first, no coin. Growth, they call it, and it's very uncomfortable.
So am I, which surprised me more than anybody. Clean manifest, for once.
